tagline: Along Washington Ridge on the old emigrant road.
intro: East of Nevada City, Highway 20 winds along Washington Ridge, and this short stretch starts at Skillman Flat. The highway largely follows the trace of the 1850 cutoff of the Emigrant Trail, which became a toll road and then a public turnpike and was still called the Old Emigrant Road. Signs of it show on either side of the pavement, and the Pioneer Trail follows sections of it beside the highway.

The gold camps on the ridge had names to suit the times. Alpha is said to have started as Hell-out-for-noon and Omega began as Delerium Tremens, and by 1880 a historian found Alpha worked out and abandoned.

moments.title: Skillman Flat
moments.text: A sawmill here burned in 1858 with 300,000 feet of lumber, and the Pioneer Trail now follows the Ridge Ditch, dug in 1857 and 1858 to carry water to the gold mines.

moments.title: Omega Overlook
moments.text: From here you can see the Alpha and Omega Diggins, a hydraulic mine once fed by Yuba River water in wooden flumes hung from granite cliffs above the river.
